description.value: The study examined BOLD activity and directed functional connectivity within the salience network during four perceptual decision-making tasks with varying difficulty.

spans.text: During four PDM tasks (1) face-house discrimination, (2) happy-angry face discrimination, (3) audiovisual asynchrony and synchrony perception, and a (4) random dot motion direction task, we varied the task difficulty and examined the interactions between these SN nodes.

design.value: Participants completed four perceptual decision-making tasks involving two-alternative choices, with task difficulty manipulated through stimulus noise, ambiguity, or coherence; fMRI BOLD activity and directed functional connectivity were assessed.

spans.text: These four tasks were commonly used in the past decade to investigate PDM processes in the brain and all of the tasks involve decisions about two alternative choices and stimulus-noise-dependent behavioral performance variations.

Experiment 1: face-house discrimination task

task_description.value: Participants discriminated faces from houses under 0%, 40%, and 55% noise.

spans.text: There were three noise-level conditions and each condition was repeated 60 times (30 times each for faces and houses)
Stimuli were presented in a random order as in an event-related design within each run.
The stimulus software presentation (www.neurobs.com) was used to display stimuli and to randomize task trial sequences.

instructions.value: indicate decisions as quickly and as accurately as possible

stimuli.value: Images of faces and houses degraded with pixel phase randomization and Gaussian noise.
